builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: GameLogicBench: Evaluating Coding Agents on Runtime Game Logic with Tick-Level State Assertions
summary: Replaces video scoring, fixed-example replay, and LLM-judged evaluation of game-development coding agents with deterministic per-tick state assertions validated by mutants that reject incomplete implementations. Costs are substantial benchmark-construction effort: 72 Godot tasks, 403 hand-designed scenarios, and mutant generation are required to make the evaluator accept varied correct implementations while rejecting faulty ones. Fails when evaluators skip mutant validation (incorrect submissions pass), when agents have open network access and copy public code, and it transfers poorly to non-game domains.
rationale: The paper is a domain-specific benchmark rather than a deployable technique, so a production engineer should adopt its design principles (execution-level assertions and mutant-validated tests) only when building agent evaluations, not the artifact itself.
technique: Tick-level runtime assertions with mutant validation for coding-agent evaluation

claims.statement: Replaces video scoring, fixed-example replay, and LLM-judged evaluation of game-development coding agents with deterministic per-tick state assertions validated by mutants that reject incomplete implementations. Costs are substantial benchmark-construction effort: 72 Godot tasks, 403 hand-designed scenarios, and mutant generation are required to make the evaluator accept varied correct implementations while rejecting faulty ones. Fails when evaluators skip mutant validation (incorrect submissions pass), when agents have open network access and copy public code, and it transfers poorly to non-game domains.
Best observed model-scaffold combination solves 52.78% of 72 tasks; evaluators built without mutant validation let incorrect agent submissions pass.
